_doc: Scenario definitions for the tests/f2 multi-peer harness.
Each scenario has:
description : human readable summary
group       : AOO group name all peers join
routing     : the TARGET routing model ('mesh' or 'matrix')
expect      : what the harness compares against TODAY (default: routing).
Use 'all-blocked' while a target model is not implemented,
and explain it in 'pending'.
pending     : optional note explaining why expect differs from routing
env         : optional env vars for every peer in the scenario
peers       : list of { name, role, advertise?, env? }
Peer role semantics (verified against the real built app):
role: null      -> no --role flag; the real app defaults to 'console'.
role: 'console' -> pass --role console (selfRole 'console').
role: 'vdi'     -> pass --role vdi (selfRole 'vdi').
advertise:false -> set SONOBUS_NO_ROLE_ADVERT=1: the peer's own selfRole
stays its default, but other peers observe 'unknown'
with hasRole=false. This is the stock-SonoBus case.
Verified ground truth (real binaries, see README 'Verified behaviour'):
3 role-less peers + SONOBUS_NO_ROLE_BLOCK=1 -> full mesh, all flags true.
role-less peer + SONOBUS_NO_ROLE_ADVERT=1   -> observed role 'unknown',
both directions blocked.
console + vdi (no env)                      -> both directions OPEN (P1.4
applies the routing matrix
on role arrival).
console + console, or vdi + vdi (no env)    -> both directions blocked
(same role).

mesh-stock.description: Pre-roles stock behaviour: three peers with no advertised role and open routing. Passes against the real app today.

matrix-1v1.description: One console and one vdi. Opposite roles, so the routing matrix opens the path both ways.

matrix-2v2.description: Two consoles and two vdis. Targets the routing matrix: console<->vdi allowed both ways, same-role pairs blocked.

blocked-unknown.description: Two peers that advertise no role at all (stock SonoBus behaviour). The matrix blocks every direction when either side is unknown, so this passes against the real app today.

matrix-target-check.description: Same peers as matrix-1v1 but compared against the TARGET matrix model. Since P1.4 this passes; kept as the explicit acceptance test for the routing matrix.

agent-health.description: One console + one VDI whose agent reports a missing input device. P1.7: the VDI attaches an 'agent' object to its peer-info JSON, and the Console must parse it, so c1's dump for v1 shows input 'missing'. The VDI's own dump reports the same health under selfAgent.

agent-silent.description: P1.7 silence detection on the REAL path: a VDI with no input override and a 2 s silence window (default is 10 min). Headless peers feed silence, so the real detector must flip input to 'silent'.

console-kind.description: P1.7 / control-api 7: Consoles advertise their kind next to role. c1 is a web Console, c2 a mac Console (both via CROSSPOINT_CONSOLE_KIND); every peer sees the right kind.
